definition: the slow process of rotting or gradually falling into a worse condition

collocations.example: Eating too much sugar is a major cause of tooth decay.
The old neighborhood showed clear signs of urban decay.

definition: settling an issue completely; having a clear effect on the final result

collocations.example: Experience was the decisive factor in the election.
The team won a decisive victory on Sunday.

definition: to take away an amount or part from a total

collocations.example: The company will deduct tax from your monthly salary.
They deduct the cost from your final bill.

definition: to consider or judge something to be a particular thing

collocations.example: The committee may deem it necessary to act quickly.
We deem it appropriate to make a public statement.

definition: a wild animal with long legs that eats grass and leaves

collocations.example: A herd of red deer crossed the quiet field.
We saw many animals in the old deer park.

definition: a fault or imperfection that makes something less than perfect

collocations.example: The baby was born with a rare birth defect.
The car was recalled due to a manufacturing defect.

definition: to delay something until a later time

collocations.example: Customers often defer payment for as long as possible.
They decided to defer the decision until next week.

definition: a lack or shortage of something that the body or a system needs

definition: to openly refuse to obey a person, rule, or authority

collocations.example: They chose to defy the law and protest publicly.

definition: easily broken, damaged, or harmed

This delicate fabric must be washed by hand.

definition: the study of human populations and how they change in size and structure

Historical demography examines population change over many centuries.

definition: to leave a place, especially to start a journey

definition: the act of leaving a place, especially at the start of a journey

collocations.example: Please check the departure time of your flight.
Passengers should wait near the departure gate.

definition: the state of needing or relying on someone or something

definition: to bring resources or a system into effective action or use

Engineers plan to deploy the new system next week.

definition: to prevent someone from having or keeping something important

definition: a feeling of having completely lost hope

A deep sense of despair filled the quiet room.

definition: the place to which someone or something is going or being sent

collocations.example: They finally arrived at their final destination at midnight.
The small island is a popular tourist destination.

definition: the things that will happen to someone in the future, seen as already decided

collocations.example: We are the masters of our own destiny.
Hard work can help you shape your destiny.

definition: to separate or unfasten something from a larger thing

collocations.example: The handle can detach from the main body.
Please detach the lower part of the form.

definition: to keep someone in official custody and prevent them from leaving

collocations.example: Police may detain a suspect for further questioning.

definition: to make someone decide not to do something, usually through fear

collocations.example: High fences deter thieves from entering the yard.
Tough penalties may deter criminals from using guns.

definition: to become progressively worse in quality or condition

collocations.example: Her health began to deteriorate rapidly last winter.
The argument could deteriorate into a serious fight.

definition: an evil supernatural being that appears in many stories and religions

definition: to plan or invent something by careful thought

collocations.example: Experts are trying to devise a plan to help.
Scientists devise an experiment to test the theory.

definition: a disease in which the body cannot properly control the level of sugar in the blood

collocations.example: He was recently diagnosed with type 2 diabetes.
People who are overweight may develop diabetes.

definition: to identify an illness or problem after examining it

collocations.example: The test is used to diagnose a variety of diseases.
Doctors can now diagnose cancer at an early stage.

definition: the act of identifying an illness or problem after examination

collocations.example: The doctor made a quick and accurate diagnosis.
Early diagnosis of cancer can save many lives.

definition: a simple drawing that explains how something works or is arranged

collocations.example: He drew a clear diagram of the engine.
The flow diagram shows each step of the process.

definition: to enter a phone number in order to make a call

collocations.example: Please dial the number slowly and carefully.
If the line is busy, dial again later.

definition: a straight line through the center of a circle, or its length

collocations.example: The pipe is ten centimeters in diameter.
Please measure the inner diameter of the tube.

definition: a very hard, clear precious stone used in jewelry

collocations.example: He bought her a beautiful diamond ring.
She wore a sparkling diamond necklace to the party.

definition: a book in which you record your personal experiences each day

collocations.example: She decided to keep a diary every day.
He wrote his secret thoughts in a personal diary.

definition: a book that lists words with their meanings and spellings

definition: to recognize or show the difference between things

Children must learn to differentiate between right and wrong.

definition: to break down food in the body so it can be used

collocations.example: Humans cannot digest plants such as grass.
Heavy, fatty meals can be hard to digest.

definition: the quality of being worthy of respect and treated seriously

collocations.example: The new law protects basic human dignity.
Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity.

definition: a difficult situation where you must choose between hard options

collocations.example: She faced a difficult moral dilemma at work.
He was in a dilemma about which job to take.

definition: not bright; giving or having little light

collocations.example: The room was lit by a single dim light.

definition: to become or make smaller, weaker, or less important

definition: a chemical compound containing two oxygen atoms joined to another element

collocations.example: Humans breathe out carbon dioxide every day.
Burning coal releases harmful sulfur dioxide into the air.

definition: to put something quickly into a liquid and take it out again

collocations.example: She dipped her toes in the cool water.
He dipped the biscuit into his hot tea.

definition: something that makes a situation less favorable or puts you in a worse position

collocations.example: Poor English can put you at a disadvantage.

definition: to get rid of something you no longer want or need

collocations.example: Please discard any old or broken clothes now.
Factories must not discard waste into the rivers.

definition: to make secret or new information known to others

definition: the act of making secret or new information known

collocations.example: The law requires full disclosure of all risks.
Public disclosure of the report caused great concern.

definition: to try to persuade someone not to do something, or to make an activity less likely to happen

collocations.example: His parents tried to discourage him from acting.
High taxes may discourage foreign investment in the country.

definition: a change of appearance used to hide who you really are

collocations.example: The spy traveled in disguise to avoid capture.
He had to wear a disguise at the party.

definition: to scatter or spread over a wide area

collocations.example: Police used tear gas to disperse the crowd.
The thick fog began to disperse quickly at dawn.

definition: to take the place of someone or something

collocations.example: New machines may displace many factory workers soon.
Clean energy could displace fossil fuels over time.

definition: to mix into a liquid and become part of it

collocations.example: Sugar will dissolve quickly in hot water.
Stir the powder until the crystals dissolve completely.

definition: to change facts or ideas so they are no longer true or fair

collocations.example: Newspapers sometimes distort the facts of a story.
The film tends to distort history for extra drama.

definition: to take someone's attention away from what they are doing

collocations.example: Loud music can distract you from your work.

definition: a feeling of great worry, sadness, or suffering

collocations.example: She was clearly in distress after the terrible accident.
The sad news caused her great distress.

definition: a share of a company's profits paid regularly to its shareholders

collocations.example: The company will pay a dividend to its shareholders.
Investors look closely at the dividend yield.

definition: relating to or coming from God or a god

collocations.example: They believed the king had divine power.

definition: an area of water where ships are loaded, unloaded, or repaired

collocations.example: Several fishing boats were tied up at the dock.
The damaged ship was repaired in dry dock.

definition: a film or program that gives facts about a real subject

collocations.example: They watched a documentary film about wild whales.
She plans to make a documentary about jazz.

definition: an intelligent sea animal with a long nose that lives in groups

collocations.example: A bottlenose dolphin swam beside the small boat.
The children enjoyed the dolphin show at the aquarium.

definition: a particular area of activity, knowledge, or responsibility

collocations.example: Space travel now lies within the domain of science.
That decision is clearly beyond my domain.

definition: a rounded roof shaped like the top half of a ball

collocations.example: The modern building has a large glass dome.
Engineers studied the dome structure very carefully.

definition: a person who gives blood or an organ to help another person

collocations.example: She is a regular blood donor at the clinic.
He signed up to be an organ donor.

definition: a small round mark or spot

collocations.example: She drew a small dot on the map.
He wore a shirt with a polka dot pattern.

definition: to fall in small drops, or let liquid fall in drops

collocations.example: Water started to drip from the broken pipe.

definition: to die from being under water and unable to breathe

collocations.example: A child can drown in very shallow water.
He nearly drowned while swimming in the rough sea.

definition: having two parts, aspects, or functions

collocations.example: She plays a dual role in the company.
The clever tool serves a dual purpose.

definition: not interesting or exciting; boring

collocations.example: The novel was a dull book I never finished.
We had to sit through a very dull meeting.

definition: the length of time that something lasts or continues

collocations.example: They stayed indoors for the duration of the storm.
The medicine works best over a short duration.

definition: to think, speak, or write about something for too long

collocations.example: There is no need to dwell on the past.
Don't dwell on your mistakes for too long.

definition: full of energy, new ideas, and the power to make things happen

collocations.example: He seemed a dynamic and energetic leader.
She has a warm and dynamic personality.

definition: a large, strong bird that hunts other animals for food

collocations.example: A bald eagle soared high above the river.
The golden eagle has sharp, powerful claws.

definition: relating to the relationship between living things and their environment

collocations.example: The dam upset the ecological balance of the river.
Scientists study the whole ecological system of the forest.

definition: a person's sense of their own importance and value

collocations.example: Winning the prize really boosted her ego.
He has a very big ego indeed.

definition: the joint in the middle of the arm where it bends

collocations.example: She hurt her elbow joint while playing tennis.
The player wore an elbow pad during the match.

definition: a tiny particle with a negative electric charge found in atoms

collocations.example: The electron microscope reveals very tiny structures.
An electron beam slowly scanned the sample.

definition: graceful and attractive in appearance or style

collocations.example: She wore an elegant black dress to dinner.
The building has a simple and elegant design.

definition: relating to the basic or first stages of a subject

collocations.example: The move from elementary school can be difficult.
Students learn elementary skills in the first year.

definition: to lift something up or make it higher

I built a platform to elevate the bed.

definition: having the right or the qualifications to do or receive something

definition: the offices of officials who represent their country in another country

definition: to be a clear and complete example or expression of an idea

collocations.example: These streets seem to embody the spirit of the city.

definition: a man who rules an empire or a group of countries

collocations.example: He studied the long life of a Roman emperor.
Visitors admired the emperor's golden throne.

definition: based on observation and experiment rather than theory alone

collocations.example: There is no empirical evidence to support his claim.

definition: to make a proposal into an official law

collocations.example: Governments should enact laws to protect the environment.

definition: to put something inside an envelope or package with something else

collocations.example: Please enclose a check with your application form.

definition: a serious and determined effort to do something

collocations.example: The mission was a great human endeavor.
The project is a fine example of scientific endeavor.

definition: to give someone or something a quality or ability

collocations.example: Herbs can endow food with subtle flavors.

definition: to make something bigger, or to become bigger

collocations.example: I want to enlarge this photo for the frame.

definition: to give someone greater knowledge or understanding of something

definition: to improve the quality or value of something

definition: to officially join or register for a course or group

definition: a thing that exists separately and has its own distinct identity

definition: a person who starts a business and takes on financial risk

collocations.example: She became a successful entrepreneur at only thirty.

definition: a feeling of wanting something that another person has

definition: the value of the shares or ownership someone holds in a company

definition: to build or put up a structure

definition: to suddenly throw out lava, ash, and gas, as a volcano does

definition: to go with someone to guide or protect them

collocations.example: Police were called to escort her off the premises.
